Arguments every chart shares

Source: R/chart-arguments.R
cd_plot_arguments.Rd

Every chart in the package (each plot() method, the equiplots and plot_comparison()) changes its text and its look in the same way, with the arguments below. They come after the arguments that say what to draw, and they have the same names as the chart options (cd_chart_options()), so what is given for one chart can be given for any other.

Arguments

title

The chart's title.

subtitle

The line under the title.

caption

The note under the chart.

x_title

The title of the horizontal axis.

y_title

The title of the vertical axis.

legend_title

The title of the legend.

...

Chart options by name (see cd_chart_options()): background, fonts, sizes, axes, grid, legend, colours. Other arguments are ignored.

options

A cd_chart_options() object or a list of chart options: a look made once, to give to several charts. Applied after the text arguments, so a text it holds wins over them.

Text

title, subtitle, caption, x_title, y_title and legend_title replace a chart's own text. NULL, the default, keeps the text the chart writes itself. To remove a text, hide it: show_title = FALSE, show_x_title = FALSE, show_legend_title = FALSE.

Look

Everything else is a chart option, given by name in ...: the background (background_color, panel_color), fonts and sizes (font_family, text_scale, title_size, axis_text_size), the axes (x_limits, y_limits, x_text_angle, flip), the grid (grid, grid_color), the legend (legend_position, legend_labels, show_legend) and the colours (colors). cd_chart_options() lists them all.

One look for several charts

Make the options once and give them to each chart as options. A chart option named in the call wins over options.

Which text is used

The six text arguments say what the chart should read; options holds what someone changed afterwards (in the apps, with the chart's customize panel), so a text in options wins over the text argument. From least to most: the chart's own text, the text arguments, options, and a chart option named in ....

Names that are gone

x_axis and x_label were other names for x_title, y_axis and y_label for y_title, and legend and fill_label for legend_title. They are no longer accepted: a chart given one stops and names the argument to use.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rates <- calculate_average_reporting_rate(data, admin_level = "adminlevel_1")

# the same arguments on any chart
plot(rates, title = "Reporting by region", y_title = "Region", legend_title = "Rate")
plot(calculate_district_reporting_rate(data, 90), title = "Districts reporting", y_title = "Percent")

# background and fonts
plot(rates, background_color = "grey95", font_family = "serif", text_scale = 1.2)

# one look for several charts
look <- cd_chart_options(font_family = "serif", background_color = "grey95", legend_position = "right")
plot(rates, options = look)
plot(calculate_district_reporting_rate(data, 90), options = look)
} # }
